newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila firms seen shopping for more corn, wheat.
newsitem.headline: Manila firms seen shopping for more corn, wheat.

text.p: Philippine buyers are expected to go back to the market for more corn and wheat next week to meet short term requirements, attracted by prospects of a further slide in U.S. wheatprices, Manila grains traders said on Friday.

"A lot of buyers are heading to the U.S. market for more wheat following its fall overnight. Manila mills are not joining the bandwagon for now, maybe next week," an executive at one Philippine mill told Reuters.
The executive said most Philippine mills were fully stocked for June after a spate of buying in the past weeks. "Orders next week will be for July," he added.
The Phippines is also expected to import more corn.
On Friday, the Philippine Association of Feed Millers sought tenders for 50,000 to 55,000 tonnes of yellow corn.
"At the bidding, the millers decided to buy U.S. yellow corn number 2," a trader who joined the tender said.
Continental Grains Co submitted the lowest bid of $137.50 per tonne C&F but the feed millers wanted a further cut.
"The feed millers agreed to give Continental until midnight to make a counter price proposal," said one trader. "If Continental cannot lower its price, there will be rebidding on Monday."
Talk in the market also said state-owned National Food Authority (NFA) has started negotiations with China for corn imports for the country's buffer stocks.
NFA officials declined comment on the rumours.
Philippine livestock and poultry farmers have asked the government to import 300,000 tonnes of corn due to a domestic shortage.
Philippine corn stocks as of May 9 dropped to 188,200 tonnes as against 237,900 in the year-ago period.
Meanwhile, rice, soymeal and soybean importers are expected to remain in the sidelines due to ample supply.
Philippine rice stocks as of May 9 reached 1.88 million tonnes compared to 1.65 million in same period in 1996.
